name: Rhode Island

sales.rateNote: Single statewide 7% sales and use tax on tangible goods, certain utility services and enumerated services. There is no general local sales tax; meals carry an extra 1% local meals and beverage tax and lodging carries state and local hotel taxes.

local.levies: no local general sales tax; a statewide 1% local meals and beverage tax (collected by the state, distributed to the city or town) and a local hotel tax apply instead
local.capNote: Not applicable: cities and towns do not levy their own general sales tax.

groceries.note: Food and food ingredients for human consumption are exempt (R.I. Gen. Laws 44-18-30(9)); candy, soft drinks and prepared food are taxable.

clothing.note: Clothing and footwear are exempt up to $250 per item; only the part of the price above $250 is taxed (a $275 coat is taxed on $25). Items normally sold as a unit, like a suit, cannot be split to qualify.

otherRates.item: meals and beverages (local meals and beverage tax)
otherRates.note: Charged by every eating and drinking establishment on top of the 7% sales tax, for 8% in total.
Hotel tax of 7% on room rentals for the first 30 days, in addition to the 7% sales tax. Since January 1, 2026 the local share rose from 1% to 2%.
New 5% whole home short-term rental tax since January 1, 2026, on top of sales tax and the 2% local hotel tax.

sales.holidayNote: No sales tax holiday found in Division of Taxation guidance for 2026.

useTax.note: Use tax of 7% on goods stored, used or consumed in Rhode Island when sales tax was not paid.

facts.text: The $250 clothing threshold applies per item: five $60 shirts bought together ($300) are all tax-free.
Restaurants may show sales tax and meals tax combined as a single 8% line if separate lines cause hardship.
Insulin and medical oxygen are exempt whether or not sold on prescription; over-the-counter drugs and dietary supplements are taxable unless prescribed.
Since January 1, 2026, the local hotel tax on all short-term rentals is 2% (up from 1%), and renting a whole home adds a new 5% tax.
Remote sellers must collect Rhode Island tax once they reach $100,000 in gross receipts or 200 transactions; Rhode Island is a Streamlined Sales Tax member state.
Lodging is taxed only for the first 30 consecutive days of a stay; a check-out restarts the count.

property.levied: local (39 cities and towns, plus fire districts); the state levies a separate Non-Owner Occupied Property Tax on high-value second homes since July 1, 2026

assessment.text: Each city or town sets assessed values as of December 31. Municipalities must perform a statistical update every third and sixth year and a full revaluation every ninth year (R.I. Gen. Laws 44-5-11.6). Rates are set per $1,000 of assessed value and can differ by class (residential, commercial, personal property).

homestead.name: No statewide homestead exemption
homestead.text: The state sets no uniform homestead exemption; tax rates and any owner-occupied treatment are decided by each city or town (some use separate rates by class, as shown in the Division of Municipal Finance's FY2026 rate table).

otherRelief.name: Non-Owner Occupied Property Tax exemptions
otherRelief.text: Homes rented long-term or as taxable short-term rentals for 183 days or more in the privilege year are exempt from the state's new tax on non-owner-occupied homes.

facts.text: Since July 1, 2026, Rhode Island taxes residential properties assessed above $1,000,000 that are not the owner's primary residence: $2.50 per $500 of assessed value above $1 million. The first payment was due September 15, 2026.
Cities and towns may not raise their total property tax levy by more than 4% over the previous fiscal year, unless an exception applies.
The motor vehicle excise tax column shows $0.00 for every municipality in the FY2026 rate table: Rhode Island cities and towns no longer tax cars.
The assessment date is December 31; the FY2026 tax roll is based on values as of December 31, 2024.
West Warwick taxes real property at four different rates depending on the type of property, an example of classified local rates.
